identity_check: Confirmed as Parallax Worlds (parallaxworlds.com), the San Francisco robotics start-up co-founded by Tanmay Agarwal (CEO) and Aumkar Renavikar (CTO) that turns phone video into simulation-ready digital twins to train and stress-test robots. Pear VC, which led its Nov 2025 seed, lists it as 'Simulation platform for testing robots before factory deployment' and links to parallaxworlds.com; three press reports of the seed name the same founders and investors. A search on the full name returned only this company, so no same-named company had to be ruled out; other 'Parallax'-branded firms were not considered because the founder gave the full name. Positioning has shifted since the raise: the homepage now sells 'AI-powered robots, production-ready in two weeks' (it ships, installs and supports robots trained in the twin) and LinkedIn calls it an 'end-to-end integrator of AI-native robots', so layer is set to 'robotics' rather than 'autonomy_tooling'. Category changed from the PROJECT_CONTEXT seed 'adjacent' to 'remote': no overlap with our procurement, maintenance, process-stability or RFQ/BOM agents; it touches only our long-term robotics / dark-factory roadmap.

company.name: Parallax Worlds
company.description: San Francisco start-up that builds digital twins from phone video to train and test robots, and now deploys trained robots on factory floors.

layer_detail: Started as autonomy tooling (hyper-realistic simulation that converts everyday video into interactive 3D digital twins, runs physics simulations with real robot software, integrates with NVIDIA Omniverse, Unreal and Unity). Now sells end-to-end robot integration: customer records a walk-through, Parallax trains the robot in the twin, then ships and installs it in about two weeks with 24/7 support; robots from OEMs such as FANUC and Standard Bots (100+ models supported). Member of A3, SEMI and ARM Institute.
product_summary: Turns a smartphone walk-through into an interactive digital twin, trains and stress-tests robots there using real robot software, then ships and installs a working robot in about two weeks with support and maintenance included, so manufacturers can automate tasks without long integration projects.
pricing: Zero Risk Policy: $0 until the robot does the task at KPIs agreed in writing; no pilot fees and no upfront hardware cost; deployment, 24/7 support and maintenance billed at a single hourly rate (rate not published).
